newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Tuesday:

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said the Commission's discussions during its Wednesday weekly meeting would focus on measures to be taken in the field of the European monetary union, adoption of a green paper on protection of minors and human dignity on audiovisual services and a communication on criminal use of the Internet.

Asked about the Commission's reaction to an advertisement in an English magazine presenting the members of the Commission as the new British government, van der Pas thanked the magazine for free advertisement but said that it was turning the great idea of European integration into division and denying the primacy of national governments.

On the issue of trans-European networks discussed during the ECOFIN Council on Monday, van der Pas said it was plausible that if the European Investment Bank came back later with the conclusion that the five key projects needed further public subsidy, the reallocation of the budget could be ipso facto reopened in the Council.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/922: Echo tv and radio awards: Commission highlights plight of victims.
- IP/96/923: SADC and EC sign regional indicative programme.
- IP/96/924: Commission clears the creation of a joint venture between Thyssen and Boehler Uddeholm.
- IP/96/925: The Phare programme at the heart of the political and economic relations between the European Community and the partner countries of central Europe.
- IP/96/926: Continued economic and political dialogue as Tacis enters a new programming cycle.
- Eurostat, statistics in focus, energy and industry No 1996-30: Producer index of industrial production.
- Memo/96/: Euro-Mediterranean partnership: implementation of the multilateral aspects of the Barcelona declaration.
